content: Terconazole is an antifungal medication used to treat vaginal yeast infections. It alleviates symptoms such as vaginal burning, itching, and discharge associated with this condition. This medication is available in cream and suppository forms, and its use is strictly for vaginal application. For the cream (8%), one full applicator should be inserted into the vagina at bedtime for three consecutive days. For the suppository (80 mg), insert one suppository into the vagina at bedtime for three days. Always wash your hands before and after application, and avoid contact with the eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse the eyes thoroughly with water. When using the cream, fill the applicator as directed in the product instructions. If using the suppository, unwrap it before insertion and use either the applicator or your finger to place it into the vagina. Lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest, insert the applicator or suppository as far as comfortably possible, and press the plunger to release the medication. Clean the applicator with warm, soapy water after use. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after one or two days. This medication can be used during menstruation, but avoid using tampons or douches while undergoing treatment. If your condition does not improve or recurs within two months, consult your doctor. Common side effects may include headaches, increased vaginal or urethral burning, itching, or pain, and menstrual cramps. Serious allergic reactions, though rare, can occur. If you experience symptoms such as fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, abdominal pain, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge, discontinue use and contact your doctor immediately. This medication may cause hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis or toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). If these occur, stop using the medication and seek medical attention. Do not resume therapy if such reactions develop. Additionally, the product is petroleum-based and may damage latex or rubber condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps. Avoid using these products during treatment and for three days after completing therapy. During pregnancy, terconazole should only be used when clearly necessary, and pregnant women should exercise caution when using the vaginal applicator. The manufacturer does not recommend its use during the first trimester. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Store the cream or suppository at room temperature. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. To prevent vaginal yeast infections, keep the genital area dry after bathing, showering, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight clothing, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp exercise clothes for extended periods. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not share it with others or use it for other conditions without consulting your doctor. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and discuss any concerns or questions about this medication.
